related_evidence.description: Multicenter validation study evaluating the diagnostic performance of the Lumipulse Plasma Ratio against CSF/PET references
FDA Class 2 Device Recall for Lumipulse G pTau217/BAmyloid 142 Plasma Ratio due to false positive and indeterminate results

evidence_assessment: The clinical evidence initially supporting the Lumipulse G pTau217/Aβ1-42 plasma ratio is robust, with large multicenter validations (e.g., BioFINDER cohorts) demonstrating high sensitivity (>97%) and specificity (>90%) for detecting amyloid pathology compared to CSF/PET gold standards. This strong performance in controlled settings supported the test's clinical utility as an accessible blood-based biomarker for Alzheimer's disease. However, real-world post-market application resulted in a Class 2 FDA recall in early 2026 due to an unexpectedly high frequency of false-positive and indeterminate results. This suggests that while the underlying plasma biomarker hypothesis remains well-validated, the specific Lumipulse assay formulation or its broader real-world implementation exhibited critical reliability issues not fully captured during clinical trials.
discrepancies: The peer-reviewed multicenter validation literature (e.g., PMID 42418465) reports high diagnostic accuracy (90.8% specificity, 97.3% NPV) and presents the assay as a reliable alternative to CSF/PET imaging. In contrast, the FDA recall document highlights a significant real-world defect causing falsely elevated positive and indeterminate results with low specificity, directly contradicting the pristine trial performance.
